question: On the current Codex application runtime, does enabling Counterlane change the verified outcome, duration, or comparable cost relative to native Codex pinned to the user's current route?
hypothesis: Counterlane Auto may retain hidden-oracle verified success while changing duration and comparable cost relative to native GPT-5.6 Sol at xhigh reasoning and standard speed.
claimBoundary: This one-task paired smoke study measures only the observed result on this exact fixture, live model catalog, sequential per-arm quota snapshots, runtime, and code build. Contaminated or noncompliant cells and paired quota/route checks remain descriptive intention-to-treat outcomes and are never token-claim eligible. It cannot establish general Counterlane efficacy or statistical confidence. The external oracle is undisclosed to the task prompt but OS-level read isolation from the model process is unverified.
experimentalUnit: A fresh copy of the same task fixture assigned to native Codex OFF or Counterlane ON on the same local Codex application runtime.

secondary: common cost when a comparable unit is available
structured input, cached-input, uncached-input, output, and reasoning-output token counts
live model-catalog parity and sequential per-arm quota snapshots
effective Counterlane route for ON; not-applicable route status for native OFF

successDefinition.verifiedSuccess: The assigned run completes, the common visible verifier passes, and the external hidden oracle passes.
successDefinition.badEscape: The assigned run completes and the common visible verifier passes, but the external hidden oracle fails.

codexRequired: live Codex App Server model catalog
effective Counterlane ON route derived from run.stdout.log; native OFF marked not applicable
reported backend reroute events for both native OFF and Counterlane ON
write-once attempt.json created before each expensive model execution

stoppingRule: Stop after native Codex OFF and Counterlane ON each start at most once and complete exactly once for every registered task. Write-once attempt markers survive crashes; missing, duplicate, rerun, or silently discarded attempts/trials invalidate the smoke packet.
